The present invention discloses a preparation method of a Cu-based resistive random access memory, and a memory. The preparation method includes: performing composition and a chemical combination treatment on a lower copper electrode (10) to generate a compound buffer layer (40), wherein the compound buffer layer (40) is capable of preventing the oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10); depositing a solid electrolyte material (50) on the compound buffer layer (40); and depositing an upper electrode (60) on the solid electrolyte material (50) to form the memory. In the above technical solution, the compound buffer layer (40) capable of preventing the oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10) is inserted between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material (50) to efficiently prevent the oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10) in a growth process of the solid electrolyte material (50), such that an electrode interface does not become rough due to the oxidation, thereby solving the technical problem of relatively low reliability and yield of the device resulting from the rough electrode interface of the Cu-based resistive random access memory in the prior art, and thus the reliability and the yield of the device are improved.

outputs.L1: The present invention discloses a method for preparing a Cu-based resistive random-access memory and a memory prepared thereby. The preparation method includes: subjecting a lower copper electrode (10) to composition and chemical combination treatment to form a compound buffer layer (40), wherein the compound buffer layer (40) is capable of preventing oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10); depositing a solid electrolyte material (50) on the compound buffer layer (40); and depositing an upper electrode (60) on the solid electrolyte material (50) to form the memory. According to the foregoing technical solution, the compound buffer layer (40), which is capable of preventing oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10), is disposed between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material (50), thereby effectively preventing oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10) during growth of the solid electrolyte material (50). Consequently, the electrode interface is prevented from becoming rough due to oxidation. This addresses the technical problem in the prior art whereby a rough electrode interface in a Cu-based resistive random-access memory results in relatively low device reliability and yield, thereby improving both the reliability and yield of the device.
outputs.L2:
The invention provides a method for manufacturing a Cu-based resistive random-access memory, as well as the resulting memory device. The method comprises subjecting a lower copper electrode (10) to compositional and chemical-combination processing to form a compound buffer layer (40) that protects the lower copper electrode (10) from oxidation. A solid electrolyte material (50) is then deposited over the compound buffer layer (40), followed by deposition of an upper electrode (60) on the solid electrolyte material (50), thereby completing the memory.

By positioning the oxidation-resistant compound buffer layer (40) between the lower copper electrode (10) and the solid electrolyte material (50), oxidation of the lower copper electrode (10) during growth of the solid electrolyte material (50) is effectively suppressed. This prevents oxidation-induced roughening of the electrode interface and addresses the prior-art problem of reduced device reliability and yield caused by rough electrode interfaces in Cu-based resistive random-access memories. Consequently, both device reliability and manufacturing yield are enhanced.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides a method for preparing copper-based resistive random access memory (RRAM), as well as the resulting memory device. In this method, a lower copper electrode is first subjected to a compositional and chemical treatment that forms a compound buffer layer on its surface. This buffer layer protects the lower copper electrode from oxidation during the subsequent deposition of the solid electrolyte material.

After the buffer layer has been formed, the solid electrolyte material is deposited over it, followed by the formation of an upper electrode to complete the memory structure. By suppressing oxidation of the lower copper electrode, the buffer layer helps maintain a smooth and stable electrode interface. This improved interface quality enhances the reliability and performance consistency of the memory device while also increasing manufacturing yield.
outputs.L4:
A copper-based resistive random access memory (RRAM) device is fabricated by first forming a lower copper electrode on a substrate. Before the solid-electrolyte layer is deposited, the exposed surface of the copper electrode is chemically treated so that a thin, oxidation-resistant copper compound is produced. This compound remains at the interface and functions as a buffer layer between the copper electrode and the subsequently deposited electrolyte.

After formation of the buffer layer, a solid-electrolyte film is deposited over the treated copper electrode, followed by formation of an upper electrode. The resulting structure comprises the lower copper electrode, the interfacial compound buffer layer, the solid electrolyte, and the upper electrode. During device operation, an applied voltage drives the migration of copper ions and the formation or dissolution of a conductive path through the electrolyte, allowing the memory cell to switch reversibly between high- and low-resistance states.

The chemical treatment protects the lower copper electrode from oxidizing during electrolyte deposition and later processing. It also suppresses undesirable reactions between the copper and the electrolyte and prevents the electrode surface from becoming rough. A smoother, more chemically stable interface promotes uniform electrolyte growth and more consistent conductive-filament formation. Consequently, the memory devices exhibit reduced cell-to-cell variation, more stable switching characteristics, and improved operational reliability. The process also decreases the incidence of defective cells, thereby increasing manufacturing yield without requiring a major change to the overall RRAM fabrication sequence.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent abstract for a preparation method of Cu-based resistive random access memory that uses a compound buffer layer to prevent oxidation of the lower copper electrode.
counterfactuals.output: A preparation method of a Cu-based resistive random access memory is disclosed. The method comprises: forming a lower copper electrode on a substrate; depositing a compound buffer layer on the lower copper electrode, wherein the compound buffer layer comprises a copper-compatible conductive sublayer and an oxygen-blocking sublayer; forming a resistance-switching dielectric layer on the compound buffer layer; and forming an upper electrode on the resistance-switching dielectric layer. The compound buffer layer is formed without exposing the lower copper electrode to an oxidizing atmosphere and prevents oxygen in the resistance-switching dielectric layer or a subsequent process from diffusing toward and oxidizing the lower copper electrode. The compound buffer layer further maintains electrical contact and regulates migration of copper ions during set and reset operations. The method reduces interfacial copper oxide formation, lowers device-to-device variation, and improves switching uniformity, endurance, retention, and manufacturing yield of the Cu-based resistive random access memory.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention for improving the reliability and manufacturing yield of Cu-based RRAM devices by inserting an anti-oxidation layer between the copper electrode and solid electrolyte.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention improves copper-based resistive random-access memory (Cu-RRAM) by inserting a thin anti-oxidation layer between the Cu active electrode and the solid-electrolyte switching layer. This interfacial layer prevents copper oxidation during fabrication and operation while permitting controlled transport of Cu ions into the electrolyte.

By preserving a clean, stable Cu/electrolyte interface, the structure enables more uniform formation and rupture of conductive copper filaments. As a result, it reduces device-to-device variability, lowers switching failures and leakage, improves endurance and data retention, and increases manufacturing yield. The anti-oxidation layer may be selected and optimized to remain electrically conductive or ion-permeable without significantly increasing operating voltage, and can be integrated using standard thin-film deposition processes.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a formal patent-style description of a Cu-based resistive memory fabrication process, including chemical treatment of a lower copper electrode, deposition of a solid electrolyte, and formation of an upper electrode.
counterfactuals.output:
## Cu-Based Resistive Memory Fabrication Process

### Technical Field

[0001] The present disclosure relates generally to nonvolatile memory devices and, more particularly, to methods for fabricating a resistive switching memory cell comprising a copper-containing lower electrode, a solid electrolyte, and an upper electrode.

### Process Description

[0002] In one embodiment, a substrate is provided having an electrically conductive feature exposed at a major surface thereof. The substrate may comprise a semiconductor wafer, an interlayer dielectric, one or more interconnect levels, and associated active or passive circuitry. The electrically conductive feature may serve as a contact to a subsequently formed resistive memory element.

[0003] A lower electrode comprising copper is formed over, and in electrical communication with, the conductive feature. The lower electrode may comprise elemental copper, a copper alloy, or a multilayer structure having a copper-containing surface layer. Formation of the lower electrode may include physical vapor deposition, chemical vapor deposition, electrochemical deposition, electroless deposition, or a combination thereof, followed optionally by lithographic patterning, etching, or chemical-mechanical planarization.

[0004] Following formation of the lower electrode, at least an exposed upper surface of the lower electrode is subjected to a chemical treatment. The chemical treatment may remove native copper oxide, organic residue, polishing residue, or other contaminants and may additionally modify the chemical composition of the copper surface.

[0005] In certain embodiments, the chemical treatment comprises contacting the exposed copper surface with a reducing or oxide-removing composition. Suitable compositions may include one or more organic acids, inorganic acids, ammonium-containing solutions, complexing agents, reducing agents, or combinations thereof. By way of example, the treatment composition may comprise citric acid, acetic acid, formic acid, hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid, ammonium hydroxide, an ammonium salt, or a copper-complexing ligand. Treatment conditions may be selected to remove surface oxide while limiting recessing or roughening of the lower electrode.

[0006] In some embodiments, the chemical treatment further comprises exposing the copper surface to a sulfur-, selenium-, tellurium-, nitrogen-, phosphorus-, or halogen-containing reactant. Such exposure may form a treated interfacial region comprising, for example, copper sulfide, copper selenide, copper telluride, copper nitride, copper phosphide, copper halide, or a non-stoichiometric derivative thereof. The treated interfacial region may be continuous or discontinuous and may have a thickness sufficient to regulate copper-ion generation and transport during operation of the memory cell.

[0007] The chemical treatment may be performed in a liquid phase, vapor phase, plasma environment, or combinations thereof. In one implementation, the lower electrode is first cleaned with an oxide-removing solution, rinsed with deionized water or an organic solvent, and subsequently exposed to a chalcogen-containing solution or vapor. In another implementation, oxide removal and surface conversion are performed substantially concurrently in a single treatment composition.

[0008] After chemical treatment, the substrate may be dried under an inert atmosphere and transferred to a deposition chamber with limited exposure to oxygen or ambient moisture. A vacuum-integrated or inert-gas transfer may be used to preserve the treated copper surface.

[0009] A solid electrolyte layer is thereafter deposited over the chemically treated lower electrode. The solid electrolyte is selected to permit field-assisted transport of copper ions and reversible formation or dissolution of a conductive filament. The solid electrolyte may comprise an ion-conductive chalcogenide, oxide, nitride, oxynitride, or combination thereof.

[0010] Exemplary solid-electrolyte materials include germanium sulfide, germanium selenide, germanium telluride, silicon sulfide, arsenic sulfide, silver- or copper-doped chalcogenide glass, silicon oxide, aluminum oxide, hafnium oxide, tantalum oxide, titanium oxide, tungsten oxide, zirconium oxide, silicon nitride, silicon oxynitride, or multilayer combinations of such materials. The solid electrolyte may be substantially amorphous, polycrystalline, or include regions of differing composition.

[0011] The solid electrolyte may be deposited by sputtering, evaporation, atomic layer deposition, chemical vapor deposition, plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition, solution deposition, or another conformal thin-film technique. In representative embodiments, the electrolyte has a thickness of approximately 2 nm to approximately 200 nm, although smaller or greater thicknesses may be employed according to the desired operating voltage, retention, and switching characteristics.

[0012] The electrolyte may be deposited as a compositionally uniform film or as a graded or multilayer structure. For example, a portion adjacent to the lower copper electrode may have a first copper-ion solubility or mobility, while a portion adjacent to the upper electrode may have a second, different copper-ion solubility or mobility. Copper may diffuse from the treated lower electrode into the electrolyte during deposition or may be introduced by a separate implantation, co-deposition, diffusion, or thermal-treatment operation.

[0013] An upper electrode is formed over the solid electrolyte. The upper electrode may comprise a material that is relatively inert with respect to copper-ion oxidation and reduction, including platinum, palladium, ruthenium, iridium, tungsten, molybdenum, titanium nitride, tantalum nitride, tungsten nitride, carbon, conductive metal oxide, or combinations thereof. Alternatively, the upper electrode may include an additional electrochemically active material where bipolar or otherwise controlled switching behavior is desired.

[0014] The upper electrode may be deposited by physical vapor deposition, atomic layer deposition, chemical vapor deposition, electroplating, or another suitable process. A barrier, adhesion, capping, or current-limiting layer may be disposed between the solid electrolyte and the upper electrode or over the upper electrode.

[0015] The lower electrode, solid electrolyte, and upper electrode may be patterned to define an individual memory cell or an array of memory cells. Patterning may be performed after deposition of each layer or after formation of a blanket electrode-electrolyte-electrode stack. A sidewall dielectric or encapsulation layer may thereafter be formed to inhibit ingress of oxygen or moisture and to restrict lateral migration of copper.

[0016] An optional thermal treatment may be performed before or after formation of the upper electrode. The thermal treatment may stabilize the chemically modified copper interface, densify the solid electrolyte, adjust the concentration or distribution of mobile copper species, or improve adhesion between adjacent layers. The thermal treatment may be carried out in vacuum or in an inert, reducing, or reactive atmosphere at a temperature below that which materially damages underlying circuitry.

### Device Operation

[0017] In operation, application of a first electrical bias between the lower and upper electrodes causes oxidation of copper associated with the lower electrode and migration of copper ions through the solid electrolyte. Reduction of the copper ions forms or extends a conductive filament, thereby placing the memory cell in a relatively low-resistance state. Application of an opposite or otherwise selected electrical bias dissolves or interrupts at least a portion of the conductive filament, thereby returning the memory cell to a relatively high-resistance state.

[0018] The chemically treated interfacial region may improve switching uniformity by controlling copper-ion injection, suppressing uncontrolled copper diffusion, reducing forming voltage, and limiting variability in filament nucleation. The disclosed process may thereby provide improved endurance, data retention, switching speed, or resistance-state separation relative to a structure formed on an untreated copper surface.

### Exemplary Method Formulation

[0019] A method of fabricating a resistive memory device may accordingly comprise:

1. providing a substrate having an exposed conductive contact;
2. forming a copper-containing lower electrode electrically coupled to the conductive contact;
3. chemically treating an exposed surface of the copper-containing lower electrode to remove copper oxide and form a chemically modified copper interfacial region;
4. depositing an ion-conductive solid electrolyte over the chemically modified interfacial region;
5. forming an upper electrode over the solid electrolyte; and
6. patterning or encapsulating the resulting stack to define at least one resistive switching memory cell.

[0020] The foregoing embodiments are illustrative rather than limiting. Individual materials, treatment chemistries, deposition sequences, and layer arrangements may be substituted or combined without departing from the scope of the disclosed fabrication process.

counterfactuals.prompt: How can oxidation-induced interface roughness be prevented during the fabrication of copper-based resistive random access memory? Provide the solution in patent abstract format with reference numerals.
counterfactuals.output: **Abstract—** A method of fabricating a copper-based resistive random access memory device **(100)** includes forming a copper electrode **(120)** over a substrate **(110)** and, without exposing the copper electrode **(120)** to an oxidizing ambient, forming a conformal oxygen-blocking interfacial layer **(130)** on a substantially planar surface **(122)** of the copper electrode. The interfacial layer **(130)** comprises an electrically conductive or field-permeable material having a thickness sufficient to inhibit uncontrolled oxidation of copper while permitting bias-induced transport of copper ions. A resistance-switching dielectric **(140)** is deposited over the interfacial layer **(130)** using a low-temperature process in which an initial nucleation stage employs an oxygen-free reactant, a remote oxidant, or a reduced oxidant dose. A counter electrode **(150)** is thereafter formed over the resistance-switching dielectric **(140)**. The copper electrode **(120)**, interfacial layer **(130)**, and at least an initial portion **(142)** of the resistance-switching dielectric are preferably formed in interconnected vacuum chambers **(200)** to prevent ambient exposure. By suppressing direct reaction between copper and oxidizing species during dielectric deposition, the interfacial layer **(130)** prevents oxidation-induced volume expansion, agglomeration, and interface roughening, thereby improving switching uniformity, endurance, and retention of the memory device **(100)**.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical abstract describing a Cu-based memory device and its preparation method, emphasizing how a compound buffer layer protects the lower Cu electrode during solid electrolyte growth and improves device reliability and yield.
counterfactuals.output: A Cu-based resistive memory device and fabrication method are described. The device comprises a lower Cu electrode, a compound buffer layer formed on the lower Cu electrode, a solid-electrolyte switching layer, and an upper electrode. The buffer layer, which may comprise a copper oxide, nitride, sulfide, or other Cu-containing compound, serves as a chemically and physically stable barrier during deposition of the solid electrolyte. It suppresses oxidation, corrosion, interfacial reaction, and plasma- or ion-induced damage to the lower Cu electrode, while limiting uncontrolled Cu diffusion and preserving a uniform electrode surface. During electrical operation, the buffer layer permits controlled Cu-ion injection into the solid electrolyte, enabling reproducible formation and dissolution of conductive filaments. The preparation method includes forming and patterning the lower Cu electrode, converting or coating its exposed surface to produce the compound buffer layer, depositing the solid-electrolyte layer under conditions that would otherwise degrade Cu, and forming the upper electrode. By stabilizing the Cu/solid-electrolyte interface and preventing electrode deterioration during growth, the buffer layer reduces leakage, short circuits, switching-voltage variation, and premature failure, thereby improving device endurance, retention, uniformity, manufacturing yield, and operational reliability.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
